Full Commentary:
Arsenal secure a 2-1 victory over Everton at the Emirates Stadium after a late winner. The Gunners went behind in the first half as Gueye's deflected free-kick found its way into the far corner after it struck the head of Rice in the wall. It took Arteta's side just a few minutes to find an equaliser after Tomiyasu arrived on the edge of the box to fire home, with the two teams going into the break at 1-1. Arsenal continued to dominate in the second half, creating 2.89 expected goals to Everton's 0.5 throughout the whole game, but they left it late to score the winner. Havertz pounced inside the box after some excellent work from Odegaard before firing into the back of the net. Despite securing the three points, the Premier League title will head to the Etihad Stadium after Manchester City won 3-1 at home to West Ham. It was an eventful final day, and the Gunners did everything they could to give themselves a chance. That's all for today, goodbye!

Everton are winless in their last 10 Premier League away games (D4 L6), failing to score more than once in any of these. It’s their longest run without an away win under the same manager since a run of 12 under Ronald Koeman between February and October 2017. No side have lost their final game of the Premier League season more often than Everton (14). However, they beat Bournemouth 1-0 last season, and are looking to win their final game in consecutive campaigns for the first time since a run of five between 2007-08 and 2011-12. The Toffees have little to play for after securing their safety a few weeks ago, but they will want to ensure they finish in 15th place above Brentford.
Arsenal go into the final day of the Premier League still in with a chance of winning the title, although they are relying on Manchester City’s result against West Ham. The last team, however, to win the top-flight title starting the final day off the top of the table was Arsenal in 1988-89, beating Liverpool at Anfield. The Gunners have won their final Premier League game of the season more often than any other side (22, including the last 12 in a row), also having the best win rate in such matches in the competition (71%). Indeed, they’ve not lost their final game of the season since 2004-05 (1-2 vs Birmingham City), and not at home since 1992-93 (1-3 vs Tottenham).

Newcastle finished in seventh position in the Premier League after a 4-2 win over Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium. The Magpies needed a win to guarantee they would finish above Manchester United and scored three goals in a brilliant first-half display. The Bees thought they had scored in the opening two minutes when Toney scored from close range, but VAR disallowed the goal for offside in the build-up. The visitors then scored three times before the break. Barnes headed in Guimaraes’ cross from the right to give them the lead before Isak assisted their second. He won possession off Pinnock and drove forward before sending a low cross towards Murphy, who slid in to score from close range. Isak then scored clinically into the bottom-left corner to give Newcastle complete control. Brentford got one back through Janelt soon after the restart, and Wissa scored an excellent goal to make it 3-2, but Guimaraes stopped their comeback with a reactive finish from close range. Newcastle created an xG of 3.41 and finished in seventh, with Brentford down in 16th. That's all for today, goodbye.

Crystal Palace end the 2023-24 season with an utterly dominant performance and a 5-0 win, against a Villa side who in truth look like they are glad the season is finished, despite their top-four finish. Mateta netted the first of his three in the ninth minute, before adding another in the 39th. Both goals were straightforward but well-taken and it meant Palace went into the break with a comfortable lead. Villa had the better of their chances in the first half, which they failed to take, time and time again. The second half started slowly, until from out of nowhere Eze added a third for the home side in the 54th minute. He fired a strong shot past Olsen before the goalkeeper had even dived! Not long after that, Mateta completed his hat trick with a tidy finish across goal, the first for Palace in the league since 2015. Eze then added to his haul with a similar finish to his first, another rocket flew past Olsen to make it five! It may have been more, had VAR not disallowed Mateta’s fourth goal. It turned out to be irrelevant anyway, as Palace ran away with the game in the end. Palace generated 2.48 xG from 15 shots, with Villa having 1.08 xG from eight shots. They finish the season with a loss, but they can find comfort in the Champions League next season. Goodbye!

The final whistle blows and Luton's time in the Premier League comes to an end with this 2-4 defeat. It's been an historic rise with lots of admirers won over the term, yet it's just not been enough. Now the Hatters return to the second division in a great financial position. Today's match just showed the difference as Fulham were ruthless even on the final day. A tense first half was summed up with a crescendo of action in the final few minutes. In the 43rd, Traore opened the scoring with a fine swivelling volley into the right of the goal. Then, Luton got one back after Bassey fouled Ogbene in the area. Morris slotted his penalty home coolly for his 11th goal of the season, yet Fulham weren't put off and, in a frenetic period, saw Jimenez fire home excellently to have the ascendency going into the break. Jimenez notched his second five minutes after the restart with a fine header off the left post, before Doughty replied with a low direct free-kick goal for 2-3. As the substitutes filtered on from both sides' fringes, Wilson put it beyond reach before the final 20 minutes. In terms of xG, Luton operated at 2.11, while Fulham outperformed their 1.06 xG with aplomb. Fulham finished 14th in the Premier League. Luton are down in 18th, yet will no doubt offer a spirited effort to get back into the big time next season. Thanks for joining us this afternoon, goodbye!

Today's referee is Matthew Donohue. 162 yellow cards and three red cards have been handed out by Donohue across his 35 games this season. Last weekend’s fixture between AFC Bournemouth and Brentford was the first Donohue has refereed in the Premier League. Luton last had a game officiated by Donohue when they defeated Wigan Athletic in an Emirates FA Cup third round replay in January 2023. The assistant referees are Ian Hussin and Wade Smith. Following their 1-0 win in the reverse fixture, Fulham are looking to complete their first league double over Luton since the 1953-54 campaign. However, Luton look to end on a high. Since their return to the Football League in 2014, the Hatters have only lost their final league game in one of their nine seasons (W6 D2), going down 3-1 at QPR in 2020-21. Fulham haven’t won their final league game in any of the last six seasons (D1 L5), since beating Sheffield Wednesday 2-1 in 2016-17.

Good afternoon everyone and welcome to this live text commentary of Luton v Fulham in Premier League final day action. Aside from a miracle here at Kenilworth Road, and a heavy Nottingham Forest defeat away at Burnley, Luton are heading back to the Championship. The 18th-placed Hatters sit on 26 points and are three points behind Forest. However, they have a 12-goal deficit working against them. Fulham have practically been on the beach for the last several weeks, finishing up in 14th. Marco Silva will still undoubtedly want a strong final day showing from his group. Rob Edwards too, will be hoping his side can give a solid performance in front of a sold-out home crowd, regardless of the permutations.

Manchester City get the job done on the final day, beating West Ham 3-1 at the Etihad to secure their fourth Premier League title in a row. A Foden double - one from well outside the penalty area and one from six yards out - within the first 18 minutes of the game gave the visitors an early and seemingly insurmountable hole to dig themselves out of, but a moment of individual brilliance from Kudus a few minutes before first-half injury time would give Moyes’ side something to cling onto ahead of the restart. Unfortunately for the outgoing coach, Guardiola’s side would quickly take a stranglehold on the second period, with Rodri sliding a finish home from outside the penalty area just before the hour to restore Manchester City’s two-goal advantage. The Hammers would struggle to offer anything offensively after conceding their third, finishing the match with an expected goals of just 0.36 - just 0.04 more than their total at half-time - compared to their opponents’ 2.01. A rather routine win on the final day sees Manchester City claim their eighth title in the Premier League era, and their fourth consecutively; an unmatched feat. The loss changes little for West Ham, who finish the season in ninth position. That concludes our commentary of the Premier League fixture between Manchester City and West Ham - we hope you’ve enjoyed it!

Everton secured their fifth consecutive Premier League win and clean sheet at Goodison Park with a 1-0 victory over the Blades. The Toffees created an xG of 1.73 in an impressive first-half display, with Doucoure denied twice by Foderingham before breaking the deadlock. A tame header was saved before the midfielder got onto the end of a cutback from Calvert-Lewin, but the goalkeeper made an excellent stop at close range. However, Doucoure then netted after brilliant work from Calvert-Lewin, who rounded Foderingham before lifting a cross to him for a simple finish. The second half failed to get going, with neither side having a shot on target. The Blades went close when Brereton Diaz got onto the end of a cross from Lowe, but he headed over. Garner then should've doubled Everton's lead in stoppage time. However, he lifted his first-time striker above the bar. Everton will end the season with a trip to Premier League challengers Arsenal, with the Blades hosting Tottenham. That's all, goodbye.

Everton deserve to be ahead at half-time after creating an xG of 1.73 from their seven shots, hitting the target five times. The Toffees have enjoyed most of the possession (59.5 per cent) and have won 57.4 per cent of their duels. Calvert-Lewin has been instrumental in the attack, controlling the ball well high up the pitch and bringing others into play, registering two key passes. As for the Blades, they have only created an xG of 0.07 in a poor first-half display. The visitors have not put Everton under enough pressure, but most of that could be put down to the Toffees brilliant defending, with Branthwaite and Tarkowski winning eight of their 11 duels combined. Brereton Diaz has been their best player since joining in January. However, he has not been involved enough. Everton are in control and have a win probability of 79.6 per cent.
Doucoure scored the only goal in the first half to give Everton a 1-0 lead over the Blades at Goodison Park. The Toffees had the best chances in the first 45 minutes, with Doucoure having two shots before scoring. The midfielder first headed a tame header straight at Foderingham before getting on the end of a cutback from Calvert-Lewin. However, his effort was stopped brilliantly by the goalkeeper. Nevertheless, he broke the deadlock in the 31st minute. McNeil found Calvert-Lewin with a throughball down the left, with the striker going around Foderingham before lifting a cross towards Doucoure, who scored an easy header from close range. Brooks then had a chance to level after tricking his way down the right side of the box, but his effort was pushed away by Pickford.

Everton have lost five of their last seven home league games against the Blades (including the previous two in a row), with the exceptions being a 4-2 win in August 1993 and a 2-0 victory in October 2006. Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.

Everton make two changes to the side that drew 1-1 with Luton in their previous Premier League match. Coleman captains the team and makes his first start since the Toffees lost 6-0 to Chelsea on April 15 and replaces Godfrey. Onana is also picked ahead of Harrison in the midfield.

The Blades are rooted to the bottom of the Premier League and are winless in their last 12 top-flight outings, losing their previous five matches. Chris Wilder's side have taken the lead in their last three fixtures against Manchester United, Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest before being comfortably beaten. United took the lead against the Tricky Trees through Ben Brereton Diaz and created an xG (expected goals) of 2.27 compared to Forest's 1.37 but were punished for missing too many chances. Callum Hudson-Odoi netted a brace on either side of Ryan Yates' goal to complete the comeback, with the winger's second strike marking the 100th time that the Blades have conceded in the Premier League this campaign. The visitors have only won three games this season and will finish on fewer than 20 points if they lose today.
Everton are unbeaten in their previous four Premier League matches and are in 15th position, 11 points above the relegation zone with just two games remaining. The Toffees secured their top-flight status against Brentford with a third straight win before a 1-1 draw with Luton Town in their last match. Dominic Calvert-Lewin put Everton ahead at Kenilworth Road with a first-half penalty, but it was cancelled out by Elijah Adebayo's leveller just seven minutes later. It has been a memorable period for the hosts, as Sean Dyche received the Premier League Manager of the Month award for April after his side collected 13 points from 18 available. Off the pitch, Everton have withdrawn their appeal against a two-point deduction for breaching Premier League financial rules.

Tottenham come from behind at home to beat Burnley 2-1, condemning Kompany’s side to the Championship in the process. Bruun Larsen gave the visitors the lead after 25 minutes with a well-taken goal thanks in large part to a fantastic Berge assist, but the relegation battlers were pegged back seven minutes later through Porro’s smashed finish. Despite the result hanging in the balance ahead of the restart, Burnley looked sapped of energy as they attempted to stop wave after wave of Spurs attack, with Muric often giving the hosts a chance to start their moves from higher up the pitch. Van de Ven would decide the result eight minutes from time with pinpoint accuracy, beating the goalkeeper at his far post with a low strike. Fully deserving of the three points after creating an expected goals of 2.5, compared to Burnley’s 0.75, Tottenham stay in fifth ahead of their penultimate match of the season against Manchester City on Tuesday. Burnley are relegated to the second division and can finish no higher than 18th, and will play their last game of the campaign next Sunday at home against Nottingham Forest. That concludes our commentary of the Premier League fixture between Tottenham and Burnley, we hope you’ve enjoyed it!

Burnley’s only chance of staying in the Premier League rests on winning this fixture, which leaves Kompany with little option but to throw players forward as the match wears on. Gudmundsson’s delivery from set-pieces and aerial ability could be utilised by the visitors, while the experience of Rodriguez could also help what is a young starting XI during moments of pressure. Tottenham also need the three points to keep the pressure on Aston Villa for the final Champions League spot, not that Postecoglou needs added reason to instruct his side to attack. Bentancur’s introduction could help the hosts control the tempo, while Lo Celso could be added to take some of the creative pressure off Maddison.
Burnley took the lead at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium but will have to be happy with a tie at half-time, as Spurs managed to pull one back to leave the two teams at 1-1 after 45 minutes. No surprise as the hosts dominated both possession and total shots, but it was Kompany’s side that were more clinical in the early stages, hitting the target with both of their first two shots; the second resulting in the opening goal of the game after Bruun Larsen latched onto Berge's threaded pass to beat Vicario. Muric's turnovers in midfield would help spark the hosts' equaliser just seven minutes later, however, with the goalkeeper constantly putting his midfield under pressure with a number of telegraphed clearances. Postecoglou's side finally found their feet towards the end of the half, with Son letting a number of strikes fly, and ended the period with a better expected goals (0.59 to 0.52) despite trailing in the metric for large parts.

It finishes 3-1 at Molineux to Crystal Palace, as Wolves struggled to deal with the pressing intensity of the visitors. An incredibly entertaining match at the City Ground is decided by a mad two minutes late in the second half, with Chelsea overturning the deficit to beat Nottingham Forest 3-2. Pochettino’s side took an early lead through Mudryk’s rolled finish, but the visitors were pegged back almost immediately by Boly’s far-post header from a Gibbs-White set-piece. The match was stretched in the second half as both teams searched desperately for a breakthrough, with Hudson-Odoi, Yates and Silva all hitting the frame of the goal. The former Chelsea winger would eventually get his angles correct however, with Hudson-Odoi curling a lovely finish into the far corner with a quarter-hour to go, giving the hosts something to hang onto. All their hard work would be undone at the 80th minute, thanks to Sterling’s close-range finish after cutting inside ahead of Aina, and the 82nd minute, when Jackson’s back-post finish into an empty net reversed the result and put the Blues 3-2 ahead. The win puts Chelsea level on points with Newcastle in sixth ahead of their penultimate match of the campaign on Wednesday, when they host Brighton and Hove Albion. Nottingham Forest are still not mathematically assured of their survival, but are three points clear of the drop and have a better goal-differential than Luton by 12. They will contest their final game of the season next Sunday, travelling to play Burnley. That concludes our commentary of the Premier League fixture between Nottingham Forest and Chelsea - we hope you’ve enjoyed it!

Despite starting strongly, it wasn't to be for Burnley, whose first half collapse cost them the game. Liverpool secure a 4-2 victory over Tottenham in the Premier League, giving themselves a glimmer of hope in the title race. It looked like it would be a comfortable game for the Reds, who produced 3.22 expected goals, when Salah headed home early on before Robertson doubled their lead just before half-time. Shortly after, Elliott's long-range strike nestled in the top corner, and it looked as though the game was over for Postecoglou and his team. However, it wasn't enough to spark a comeback for the away side as the Reds held on to secure a 4-2 victory. Tottenham struggled to create throughout, producing just 1.16 expected goals, and they will face Burnley next as they continue to fight for a European spot. Tottenham Hotspur are looking to complete their first league double over Liverpool since the 2010-11 season, beating two different Reds managers that campaign (Roy Hodgson and Kenny Dalglish). Their last league double over the Reds beating the same manager twice was in Dalglish’s first spell in 1986-87. Ange Postecoglou’s side currently find themselves sitting in fifth place in the Premier League table, seven points behind Aston Villa in fourth. Tottenham haven’t lost any of their last six away Premier League games on a Sunday (W2 D4), with their last such defeat coming at Anfield against Liverpool in April 2023.
As the Premier League title chase nears the finish line, Liverpool continue their pursuit of Arsenal today. The Reds sit in third place on 75 points, five points behind the Gunners in first place. Jurgen Klopp’s side have lost their last two home games in all competitions, as many as in their previous 57 combined. Somehow, a wide-open first half of two halves ends goalless at Old Trafford, as Manchester United and Burnley head down the tunnel still on level terms. After United threatened to open the scoring on several occasions, with the influential Bruno Fernandes striking the goal-frame, the Clarets bit back, and only some slack finishing and Onana's heroics have kept them from going in front. The visitors' xG stands at 0.84 to their hosts' 0.94, but given how momentum swung so far in their favour, Kompany's relegation battlers may feel they should have a lead to protect. While the live win-probability calculator rates their chances of victory at just 18 per cent, Burnley can be heartened by the manner of their revival. It's another uneven performance from Man Utd.

Relegation-threatened Burnley make the short trip to Manchester in need of points to aid their quest for top-flight survival. Vincent Kompany's side have belatedly revived hopes of avoiding an immediate return to the Championship, and last week's 4-1 success over Sheffield United put the Clarets within three points of escaping the drop zone. Wolves prevailed against Luton Town at Molineux thanks to a 39th-minute goal from Hwang Hee-Chan and an eventually decisive second from Toti five minutes into the second half. Carlton Morris did manage a riposte for the visitors with 10 minutes left, yet a relatively dominant second-half display from the hosts was enough to snuff out any comeback from the Hatters. Wolves continue in the right direction towards the Premier League's top 10 with three games to go. However, Luton Town have it all to do if they're to survive as they stay 18th and a point behind Nottingham Forest. The first goal was well-worked by Hwang. Bettering his constant sparring partner in Teden Mengi, he jinked and jived in from the left to fire across Kaminski's goal. It may've been helped on its way by Mengi, yet the Korean isn't likely to care with his 11th of the season, and his first goal in the Premier League since December 2023. Toti's goal came from a short corner routine on the right. Mario Lemina lofted over the received pass and found his Portuguese defender who nodded home strongly. While Luton were relatively uninspiring after this, they were boosted by the re-introduction of Elijah Adebayo and he helped cause chaos in the build-up to Luton's goal. Doughty put in a corner the big forward won, and at the second time of asking, he then floated a ball for Reece Burke to head for Morris to drive home on the volley. Wolves denied Luton in the final exchanges, and came good on an xG of 1.08 in comparison to the Hatters' 0.42. Now, Wolves look onwards to a trip to the Etihad Stadium next Saturday, while Luton will monitor Forest's result against Manchester City before they welcome Everton to Kenilworth Road on Friday. Bournemouth lead Brighton here at half-time thanks to Marcos Senesi's headed opener from close range in the 13th minute. While a relatively even and scrappy game has broken out in the middle of the Vitality's pitch, it must be said that Bournemouth hold more of an offensive edge. Darting wingplay, mixed with a high press from Iraola's side has put Brighton under a lot of undesired pressure with very little response. The corner wasn't cleared and the ball popped up nicely for the Argentine to head home with ease. Number five arrived four minutes from time, as Schade put it into trouncing territory. Berry grabbed one back after a Janelt mistake, yet with four games to go - it’s a meagre offering in comparison to the Hatters’ survival aspirations. Edwards’ men admittedly still remain in the mix, with attention turning to their next game away at Wolves where ideally they'd look to better their 0.54 xG. In the meantime, eyes will certainly be glued to tomorrow’s clash between Everton and Nottingham Forest for a little help going into a tense finale at the foot of the table. Burnley have had a slight upturn in form and have only lost one of their last six Premier League fixtures, but Vincent Kompany will be thinking his side should have more points on the board after their previous two outings (winning one and losing one). It has been a period to forget for Arijanet Muric, who gifted Dominic Calvert-Lewin the winning goal in a 1-0 loss to fellow strugglers Everton before scoring a calamitous own goal to help Brighton claim a 1-1 draw at Turf Moor, with the Clarets ahead at the time. As a result, Burnley would've been right behind 17th-placed Nottingham Forest but are instead six points from safety. A repeat of their 5-0 win over the Blades in the reverse fixture would boost confidence levels. However, anything else would make it difficult for them to escape relegation with just a handful of matches remaining, especially with three of the top seven and Forest left to play.
The Blades' winless run in the Premier League extended to eight games after a 2-0 loss to Brentford in previous last outing, with their last victory coming against relegation rivals Luton Town in February. Chris Wilder's men did collect respectable draws against Bournemouth, Fulham and Chelsea. However, they must quickly turn one point into three to stand any chance of climbing off the bottom of the table and avoid an immediate return to the Championship. United are 10 points from safely with just six games remaining and face a Burnley side just four points and one place above them. It's a must-win match for the Blades, who face trips to Manchester United and Newcastle United next.

A goal in either half gives Arsenal a much-needed win after a difficult week, with the Gunners deserved 2-0 winners against Wolves at Molineux, producing an expected goals of 1.21 compared to O’Neil’s side’s 0.14.  Despite going into the interval behind by a goal thanks to Trossard’s sliced shot from 18 yards out, Wolves did not appear to respond after the restart, allowing their opponents to see even more of the ball in an attempt to control the tempo and see out the result. Things picked up for the hosts after the introductions of Sarabia and Lemina after 50 and 70 minutes respectively - the latter playing as a forward - but Wolves left themselves too much to do by that stage. Raya had a single save to make in the second half, a comfortable stop from Lemina’s curling effort, while Arsenal fired 16 shots in that time, with Odegaard doubling the visitors’ advantage two minutes from time with an accurate strike from a difficult angle. The two-goal advantage is enough to see Arsenal once again go first in the table, ahead of a London derby with Chelsea on Tuesday, while Wolves stay 11th and host Bournemouth on Wednesday. That concludes our commentary of the Premier League fixture between Wolves and Arsenal - we hope you’ve enjoyed it!

It's a brilliant win for Crystal Palace, who finish 5-2 up at home, having thoroughly outclassed a dismal West Ham. They were 4-0 up within half an hour thanks to the combined efforts of sensational wingers Olise and Eze, as well as an own goal by Emerson and the first of two for top scorer Mateta. The latter secured his brace 15 minutes into a less eventful second half, with only Antonio’s goal shortly before half-time and an embarrassing slip-up and own goal by goalkeeper Henderson in the dying moments of the game marring an otherwise excellent day for Glasner’s side. The Eagles finish with an xG of 2.47 and five goals to show for it, compared to 1.27 for West Ham, who missed the chance to move up into sixth. Palace had won just five of their previous 40 London derbies but have added an imperious win to that list, moving 10 points clear of the drop zone and recording back-to-back victories for the first time this season. As we’ve come to expect in the last few years, Pep Guardiola’s City side enter this game in absolutely imperious form. They’ve not lost since early December and have won their last seven straight matches – all by two goals or more. If they make it eight in a row with another three points against Spurs, they’ll go above Tottenham’s bitter rivals Arsenal at the top of the table ahead of the season’s final round of fixtures.
It’s a must-win match for Tottenham too, though, who simply have to take maximum points from this game if they’re to have any chance of beating Aston Villa to fourth place on the final day. Spurs snapped a four-game losing streak with a 2-1 win over Burnley last time out, relegating the Clarets in the process, but now face an entirely different proposition in the form of Manchester City.

Tonight's fixture is all about firming up places in Europe next season and it's all a little messy, so let's try and break it down. Manchester United can still take the one remaining Europa League spot by winning the FA Cup, which would mean the team finishing sixth - which is currently Newcastle - would go into the Europa Conference League. If, however, Man United lose to Manchester City in the FA Cup final then the team finishing sixth goes into the Europa League and the Europa Conference League berth goes to the team in seventh, which is currently Chelsea. To make things more complicated, Newcastle and Chelsea can still overhaul Tottenham to take fifth - a spot that guarantees Europa League football - though Spurs place Sheffield United on the last day. Okay, all clear? Probably not, but just trust the fact this one is about European football permuations...
Newcastle, meanwhile, are finishing the campaign pretty strongly. Eddie Howe's men have lost just once in their past six, winning four of those and drawing their last fixture 1-1 with Brighton. You'd have to say they probably start this one as slight favourites.

It ends all square at the City Ground, as another pair of quick-fire goals midway through the second half ensure the spoils are shared! Forest took the lead for the first time with their first real chance of the second period, with Danilo on hand to finish off a scrappy move after Gibbs-White had twice looked to have lost the ball in the box. Bournemouth and Manchester United share the spoils with a 2-2 draw at the Vitality Stadium. The Cherries opened the scoring in the first half through Solanke, with his powerful shot flying into the bottom corner from outside of the box, leaving Onana with no chance. Iraola's side pushed for the second, but against the run of play, Fernandes popped up in the penalty area to volley in an equaliser from just a few yards out. It didn't take long for Bournemouth to get back in front, as Kluivert drifted in from the right-hand side to fire in at the near post before half-time, with the Cherries going into the break with a narrow lead. In the second half, Iraola's men looked threatening in the final third, but United were awarded a penalty after Smith handled inside the box, and Fernandes tucked it away to equalise for United. There was almost late drama as Bournemouth were given a stoppage-time penalty, but after a VAR review, the officials decided that the foul was committed outside of the area. Ten Hag's side have now won just once in their last seven Premier League games, while the Cherries, who finished with a higher xG (1.75 to 1.18), extend their unbeaten run at home to four matches. Fulham ended a poor recent run of away form with a 2-0 victory over West Ham at London Stadium. The visitors recorded a league double over the Hammers for just the third time thanks to an early goal against the run of play by Pereira. It arrived after a number of half chances weren't capitalised upon by the hosts, and was actually Fulham's first shot of the game. Iwobi flighted a ball over from the right to Muniz, yet thanks to Mavropanos' tame interception - Pereira could latch on and dribble round Fabianski to smash home nine minutes in. For Moyes' West Ham, their meagre xG output of 1.07 will need to be pushed if they are to overturn their quarter-final deficit against Leverkusen on Thursday. While we thank you for joining us today, it's worth extending our best wishes to young George Earthy following his head injury today which led to the extended stoppage time. Thank you and goodbye.

Aston Villa secure a crucial 2-0 victory over Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium, denting the Gunners' Premier League title hopes. The North Londoners created 1.62 expected goals throughout, while Emery's side produced 1.13. There were plenty of chances in the first half, with Watkins striking the post and Trossard denied by Martinez from just a few yards out, but the two sides went into the break level at 0-0. Arteta's men struggled to create too many opportunities in the second half and Villa remained patient, sitting deep while looking to hit their opponents on the counter-attack. The Villans eventually broke the deadlock in the 84th minute, as Bailey arrived at the back post to fire into the net after a dangerous cross from Digne. Just a few moments later, Tielemans sent a searching ball over the top of the Arsenal defence for Watkins to run onto, and the English forward lifted it over Raya to make it 2-0. The home side threw everything at it in the final stages, but they couldn't get back into the match. With Liverpool losing earlier today, it was the ideal opportunity for the Gunners to take a huge step in the title race, but they failed to take advantage. Villa now go three points clear of Tottenham, who sit in fifth place. That's all for today, goodbye!

Only one goal to speak of in the second period, but what a half it proved to be, with chances galore at both ends. Not the most spectacular of games tonight, with both sides claiming a point from a 0-0 draw. That point will be more important to Brentford, looking anxiously over their shoulder at their relegation rivals, than to Brighton, who really should have done better given their dominance. Brentford looked tired throughout, probably thanks to their exertions at the weekend, although they did well to frustrate the Seagulls’ attack. Brighton controlled much of the game, only occasionally looking vulnerable on the break, having 67 per cent possession and the stronger xG of 1.11 to the Bees’ 0.50. Injury time in both halves provided the game’s main talking points: Brighton were denied an extremely weak shout for a penalty at the end of the first, while Welbeck’s extremely near miss in the dying throes of the game added some late drama (and really should have snatched all three points). Brentford take on Aston Villa next, while Brighton face current leaders Arsenal. Thanks for reading!

There we have it, it's full-time and Manchester City run out 4-1 victors against Aston Villa. In all honesty, the first half was pretty well matched as Rodri's excellently taken opener was cancelled out by Duran. But then the brilliant Foden took over. His first goal was a lovely free-kick, but Zaniolo will rue stupidly moving out of the wall to allow it to happen. After the break, though, it was the Foden show. The England man finished coolly from Rodri's lay-off then rounded out the hat-trick with a brilliant effort into the top-right corner - City's dominance reflected by an xG of 3.28 to Villa's 0.73. It was a win City needed after that Arsenal stalemate at the weekend, especially with the Gunners defeating Luton Town 2-0. The end result of the evening is that Arsenal are top of the table with 68 points, while City are a point back in third and level with Liverpool, who face Sheffield United on Thursday.

Burnley got their first win since before Christmas before the international break, beating 10-man Brentford 2-1 to end an 11-match winless run in all competitions (D3 L8). The Clarets are still five points below Luton Town in 17th place, but another win here would certainly give them a boost in the relegation fight. However, Burnley are one of three teams yet to win successive Premier League games this season (along with Crystal Palace and Sheffield United), and they haven't done so since April 2022, when they managed three in a row.
Chelsea still have an outside chance of booking a place in Europe next season, and a win here could move them into the top half of the table if results around them also go their way. The Blues are unbeaten in their four outings in all competitions since losing the EFL Cup final to Liverpool (W3 D1) and booked another trip to Wembley last time out as they beat Leicester City 4-2 to reach the FA Cup semi-final. Their home form is good too, having lost just one of their last 14 games at Stamford Bridge in all competitions (W10 D3).

And breathe! An incredible six-goal thriller ends in a 3-3 draw between Sheffield United and Fulham at Bramall Lane. It was a game of two highly contrasting halves. Fulham dominated so much of the possession in a goalless first-half, during which they missed a host of chances. Right from the get-go, the second-half seemed like it had all the ingredients to turn this into a thriller. The Blades took the lead out of nowhere, Fulham equalised in quick time, before United went 3-1 up. For the second time in as many games, they saw a two-goal lead slip, and it was that man Muniz again for Fulham who hit home the equaliser with a ‘goal of the season’ contender. Sheffield United earn another point but are still seven points from safety ahead of facing Liverpool next. Fulham, who face Nottingham Forest next, stay in 12th place with 39 points. Until next time, goodbye!

It's all over in north London, as Spurs come back from 1-0 down to defeat Luton late on, thanks to a timely strike from their captain Son! Despite Luton pressing for an early goal to match Chong's strike in the first half, it was Spurs who got themselves level just six minutes into the second period. Vicario saved Barkley's shot at one end, and within seconds, Johnson's enticing cross from the right was unfortunately turned into his own net by Kabore! Spurs continued to press for a winner through Son, Werner, Porro and Johnson, while Clark went closest for Luton at the other end. All would be denied by Kaminski and Vicario in the respective nets, until the hosts rallied with just four minutes left on the clock. Werner's cross was steered into Son's path by Johnson, and the Tottenham captain smashed home the winner to spark pandemonium in the stands! The hosts held on to secure a 2-1 victory which returns them to the winners' circle, while Luton's wait for three points in the Premier League extends beyond the two-month mark. Spurs are back in fourth – for now – while Luton's late defeat sees them drop back into the relegation zone as the final home straight of the season continues.

Villa have lost three of their last four Premier League matches at Villa Park and were far from their best in the first half. The hosts only created an xG of 0.31 from their four attempts, with Diaby thumping in the opener with a first-time shot from outside the box. Diaby scored the only goal in the first half to give Villa a 1-0 lead over Wolves at Villa Park. The Old Gold started strongly and were punished for missing their chances. Doyle flashed a shot from the edge of the box just wide of the left post before Ait-Nouri had a huge opportunity to break the deadlock. Bueno's cross from the right dropped straight to his feet, but the Algeria international struck his effort straight at Martinez from close range. The Lions slowly built their way into the half and ended strongly. Tielemans slid a perfect throughball into the path of Watkins, but the forward slammed the side of the net. Torres then had a header saved before the hosts took the lead. Luiz chipped a free-kick down the left to Bailey, who cut the ball back to Diaby on the edge of the box. Muniz's brace helps Fulham to a 3-0 victory over Spurs. Spurs struggled to get going in the first half, and they were punished for an even slower start to the second as Fulham tripled their lead within the first 16 minutes. Lukic scored his first goal for the club with a close-range tap-in before Muniz got his second of the game just after the hour-mark when he bundled it over the line. They were denied a fourth moments later by the flag, as Palhinha's shot deflected in off Jimenez, who was offside. Postecoglou made changes, and they attempted to fight back, but Werner fired wide from two yards out, with Richarlison also missing a late chance to get a consolation. Fulham stay 12th but are now just two points off the top half of the table, and they'll travel to Sheffield United in their next game after the international break. Spurs miss out on the chance to move fourth and leapfrog Villa, who could reopen the gap to fifth to five points tomorrow. They host Luton Town next time out. That's all for today, goodbye!

Arsenal’s 5-0 dispatching of Chelsea yesterday heaps the pressure back on Liverpool, who must win at Goodison Park to go back level with the Gunners at the top of the Premier League table. The Reds responded to a shock home loss to Crystal Palace by beating Fulham 3-1 in clinical fashion on April 21st, and having been dumped out of the Europa League by Atalanta, Jurgen Klopp’s side will be throwing everything they’ve got at Everton in the German’s final title race.

Spurs have only lost one of their last seven Premier League matches, but there are still plenty of things to improve for Ange Postecoglou's men if they want to stand a chance of finishing in the top four this campaign. The visitors haven't won back-to-back matches in the top flight since December (where they won three in a row) and haven't kept a clean sheet in their last nine games. Additionally, the Lilywhites have conceded first in their previous four league outings but came from behind to beat a spirited Crystal Palace side in their last fixture. Eberechi Eze opened the scoring for the Eagles with a sublime second-half free-kick before Tottenham turned it around with goals from Timo Werner, Cristian Romero and Son Heung-min. If Spurs can win for just the second time in seven matches on the road in the Premier League, they will go two points behind Villa and have control of their destiny due to having a game in hand on their opponents.
Villa went through a rocky patch in the Premier League and only won one of their first four matches in 2024, disrupting their charge towards qualification for next season's Champions League. However, the Lions have improved their form and have won three successive games in the top flight. After triumphs over Fulham and Nottingham Forest, it looked like Villa were easing their way to another victory when they were 2-0 ahead at half-time. Yet, second-half strikes from Tahith Chong and Carlton Morris for the Hatters set up an enthralling finish. Despite Luton's impressive comeback to level the score, Unai Emery's side prevailed thanks to Lucas Digne, who netted an 89th-minute winner for Villa. The hosts are five points above fifth-place Tottenham, so they will strengthen their grip on a place in fourth if they can beat a direct rival. Although, Villa might be slightly more tired than their opponents after travelling to Ajax for a 0-0 draw in the first leg of their Europa Conference League last-16 tie in midweek.

Brighton, meanwhile, have somewhat atone for the midweek thrashing by Roma with a decent performance in the opening period.
Brighton lead 1-0 here at a drizzly American Express Stadium but not thanks to a Brighton player. That's right, while Forest haven't found favour at the top end of the pitch, they've managed to beat their own keeper. That's not to say the hosts hadn't been dangerous. Omobamidele capped an unfortunate sequence with an own goal on the 29th minute. He gave away the initial foul on Fati and was unlucky to get in the way of his shot-stopping teammate as he came for the ball. Forest wanted a foul on the goal line, but it never came. Instead, they converted this season's 32nd own goal in total. Although they looked promising in response, it's been a case of missing the final ball. Brighton's xG sits at 0.38 after that period. For Forest, they'll look to vastly improve on an xG of 0.16.

City would have been frustrated to drop two points in the reverse fixture between these sides at the Etihad Stadium in November, when Trent Alexander-Arnold's strike cancelled out Erling Haaland's opener. That draw came in the midst of a difficult run for the champions, but they enter this match unbeaten in 20 outings across all competitions, winning 18 of those games. They booked their spot in the UEFA Champions League quarter-finals in midweek and were able to rest a few players in their 3-1 win over Copenhagen, and with Liverpool still battling an injury crisis, they will view this game as a big opportunity to take control of the title race and lead from the front.
We're approaching the final stretch in one of the most absorbing title races in Premier League history, with three teams still vying to top the pile. Arsenal are currently at the summit after their hard-fought 2-1 win over Brentford on Saturday, but both Liverpool and City know a victory here would take them into top spot. It's always a massive occasion when teams managed by Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola do battle, and this match has the added significance of being their final Premier League meeting before the German leaves Liverpool at the end of the season. An incredible atmosphere is surely in store – will the Anfield factor help the Reds land a blow in the title race?

With Manchester City and Arsenal not playing today, Liverpool can move four points clear at the top of the league ahead of their games. They've won just two of their 11 games since the start of 2024 (D4 L5), with only one of those victories coming in the league, though that was in their last home match against 10-man West Ham (2-0). After letting a two-goal lead slip and then looking likely to concede a third, Aston Villa steal maximum points with a late winner at Kenilworth Road, leaving Luton Town empty-handed despite their superb second-half revival. The Villans were cruising thanks to Watkins' brace before the break, but their hosts fought back strongly, as Chong and Morris replied, following a barrage of crosses and set-piece deliveries from Luton's widemen. Finally, substitute Digne slipped free to head home Villa's third goal, which lifts them five points clear of Tottenham in the race for a top-four finish - albeit having played one game more. Meanwhile, the Hatters remain four points adrift of safety, ahead of next week's visit to fellow strugglers Crystal Palace. Having escaped with victory today, a big week lies ahead for Aston Villa, who visit Amsterdam for a Europa Conference League tie with Ajax before hosting Spurs three days later. That's all from our live Premier League coverage, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Although goals either side of half-time briefly threatened an improbable Nottingham Forest fightback, Aston Villa ultimately capitalise on a three-goal advantage to win 4-2 at Villa Park and boost their hopes of a top-four finish. Moving further clear of Manchester United and Tottenham in that respect, Unai Emery's side took control through an early Watkins strike and a Douglas Luiz double, before Forest reduced their deficit via Niakhate and Gibbs-White. Dunk powered in a 95th-minute header to help 10-man Brighton earn a point against Everton in a 1-1 draw at the Amex Stadium. Jurgen Klopp's side bounced back from their 3-1 defeat at the Emirates Stadium by beating Burnley by the same scoreline last week, but they come into this game with a few selection issues, with the likes of Alisson, Trent Alexander-Arnold and Dominik Szoboszlai out. Yet another brilliant Arsenal display sees them run out dominant winners at Turf Moor as they hammer hapless Burnley 5-0. The visitors were ahead after just four minutes as Odegaard rifled home from Martinelli's cutback, and it was 2-0 with four minutes to go until the break, Assignon bringing down Trossard before Saka squeezed the resulting penalty past Trafford and in. Any hopes of a Burnley comeback were ended just moments after the break as Saka thumped home, before Trossard netted to make it 4-0. Havertz rounded off the scoring with 78 minutes on the clock with a brilliant solo effort, weaving into the box before coolly finishing. A sixth straight win for Arsenal means they go two points off leaders Liverpool, while their +11 goal difference over the last two games means that Manchester City would have to beat Chelsea by five goals later on Saturday to leapfrog the Gunners into second. For Burnley, they remain seven points off safety, and relegation looks an increasingly looming prospect. They have a crucial game away at fellow strugglers Crystal Palace next Saturday, while Arsenal play on Wednesday away at Porto in a Champions League round-of-16 first leg. Bournemouth’s form completely opposes that of Newcastle. The Cherries looked to have recovered from a poor start to the season in December, with their Boxing Day victory over Fulham being their sixth win in seven games. However, Andoni Iraola’s men have stumbled since then and are without a victory in their last five top-flight outings (losing three and drawing two). Bournemouth lost 3-1 to the Cottagers in their previous fixture, slipping to 13th in the table, eight points clear of the relegation zone. Back-to-back matches versus Newcastle and Manchester City will make it difficult for the Cherries to end their poor run. As a result, the visitors will be looking at the start of March as an opportunity to turn their fortunes if they cannot secure a win in their next two, with matches against Burnley, Sheffield United and Luton Town.
Newcastle had lost four successive Premier League matches but have now won two of their last three top-flight fixtures to move up to seventh in the table, just five points behind Manchester United in sixth. The Magpies have been in some enthralling fixtures, ending Aston Villa's 17-match unbeaten run at home before coming from behind to draw 4-4 with Luton Town at St. James' Park. Eddie Howe's men then beat a resurgent Nottingham Forest 3-2 at the City Ground in their previous outing, resisting two equalisers from the Tricky Trees to win. Champions League football might be out of Newcastle's reach, with the hosts 11 points behind fourth-placed Tottenham, but a place in Europe still looks likely. However, the Magpies must improve defensively, as they have conceded 16 goals in their last six games.

Liverpool move back to the top of the Premier League table with a 3-1 win over Burnley at Anfield. The Clarets were the better side in the opening exchanges, but Liverpool scored the opener through Jota, who headed in Alexander-Arnold’s corner after Trafford failed to deal with it. O’Shea then powered in a header just before half-time, but the visitors couldn't build any momentum after the restart. Elliott came off the bench and played a vital role in the Reds’ further two goals. First getting down the right side of the box, he waited for options before finding Diaz, who bundled in a header from close range. The substitute then lofted a cross from the right over to Nunez, with the striker powering a downward header past Trafford. The Clarets had opportunities earlier in the second half when they were one goal behind, but they lacked a clinical edge. Fofana twice went one-on-one with Kelleher. However, he crashed his first effort straight at the goalkeeper before curling his strike wide second time around. Next up, Liverpool travel to Brentford in the Premier League, with Burnley hosting Arsenal.

Burnley centre-back O'Shea powered in a header just before half-time to net a deserved equaliser against Liverpool and send the teams into the tunnel with the score 1-1. The Clarets had the better chances in the opening exchanges, with Amdouni going the closest. He drove down the left with the ball, but his strike from close range was blocked by Kelleher. The Reds then took the lead with their first effort on target. Alexander-Arnold's outswinging corner wasn't dealt with by the onrushing Trafford, allowing Jota to head in for a simple opener. Diaz's first-time strike was then saved well by the Clarets' goalkeeper before the visitors levelled. Brownhill's corner from the right was met by O'Shea, who escaped Endo and crashed his accurate header into the top-right corner.

Gross' penalty gives Brighton a 1-0 lead over Tottenham at half-time. The visitors started brightly, with Vicario forced into action after just 47 seconds to deny Welbeck's curling effort. Roberto De Zerbi makes five changes to his side after their big win over Palace last Saturday, but won't be on the sidelines himself. There's a change in goal, with Steele coming in, and Estupinan, Lallana, Welbeck and Mitoma, who is also back from the Asia Cup, also starting. Verbruggen and Ferguson drop to the bench, while Igor Julio, Joao Pedro and Jack Hinshelwood aren't in the squad.
Ange Postecoglou makes just two changes from the draw with Everton last time out, with Sarr and Kulusevski both being brought in. Hojbjerg and Johnson start on the bench, as do Son and Bissouma now that they're back from the Asia Cup and Africa Cup of Nations.

As for Brighton, they're looking to win back-to-back league meetings against Spurs for the very first time, and another victory here would lift them up to sixth in the table. Following that game, Brighton actually went winless in three Premier League games and failed to score in all of them, but they put that right last time out, cruising to a 4-1 victory over rivals Crystal Palace last Saturday.
With Aston Villa not playing until tomorrow, Spurs have a chance to move back into the top four with a win here today. Since losing to Brighton 4-2 in the reverse fixture in December, they've lost just once in all competitions - a 1-0 defeat to Manchester City that knocked them out of the FA Cup. In the Premier League, they're unbeaten in four matches (W2 D2), but were denied three points last weekend by Jarrad Branthwaite's stoppage-time equaliser in a 2-2 draw with Everton.

Newcastle claim a huge 3-2 win at Forest and climb back into the top seven! The Magpies avenge their home defeat to the same side but were really made to work for it. Howe's side led three times, with Guimaraes, who netted the opener, proving the matchwinner. Elanga cancelled out Guimaraes' first, then Hudson-Odoi responded to Schar's fine strike. Man Utd boost their top-four hopes in the Premier League after a battling 2-1 victory over Villa on the road. Having watched Chelsea dump them out the FA Cup in midweek, Villa Park was once again disappointed when Maguire towered above Kamara from Fernandes’ corner to tee up Hojlund’s 17th-minute opener. That marked Hojlund’s fifth straight top-flight game that he has scored in before McGinn, Watkins and Ramsey all tested Onana in response to the early strike from the away side. Watkins was again denied by the United goalkeeper after the interval, only for Luiz to crash into the roof of the net to equalise after 67 minutes from Diaby’s hopeful right-wing centre. Luton are in good form in the Premier League and have won three of their last five matches to take themselves out of the relegation zone and into 17th position. Securing two consecutive triumphs over Newcastle and Sheffield United at the start of the run, the Hatters lost 3-2 to Chelsea before collecting a point against Burnley. However, Rob Edwards' men returned to winning ways with their most emphatic win of the season in their previous match, with a hat-trick from Elijah Adebayo and a goal from Chiedozie Ogbene helping them secure a 4-0 win over European hopefuls Brighton. It was a special victory for Luton, with captain Tom Lockyer making his first appearance at Kenilworth Road since suffering a cardiac arrest in December's game at Bournemouth. The visitors will now be looking to complete a famous double over Newcastle for the first time since the 1937-38 campaign.
Newcastle ended a four-match losing run in the Premier League with a 3-1 win over Aston Villa in their last outing. The Villans had won 16 of their previous 17 games at home in the top flight, but a brace from Fabian Schar and an own goal from Alex Moreno helped the Magpies to a comfortable three-goal lead before Ollie Watkins netted a consolation. A third straight-away victory in all competitions lifted Eddie Howe's men into eighth position. Newcastle are 14 points behind fourth-placed Tottenham, meaning their chances of qualifying for the Champions League for the second successive season is very unlikely. However, they will still be hoping that a place in the Europa League or Europa Conference League is in their grasp. Despite this, the Magpies must improve their form at St. James' Park, with the hosts losing back-to-back fixtures against Nottingham Forest and Manchester City.

Aston Villa have stormed back into the top four of the Premier League with a 5-0 hammering of Sheffield United at Bramall Lane. The Villans suffered their first home defeat in almost a year in midweek against Newcastle, but have issued the perfect response. Unai Emery's men did the majority of the damage in the first half, scoring four goals in 30 minutes. John McGinn broke the deadlock before Ollie Watkins produced a clinical finish for the second. VAR denied the Blades a consolation goal in stoppage time to chalk off Vinicius Souza's effort, which summed up a torrid day for Chris Wilder's men. Sheffield United face a huge game against Luton on the road in their next outing, while Villa take on Chelsea in a fourth-round replay in the FA Cup at Villa Park on Wednesday.

Aston Villa's Premier League title ambitions have taken a huge hit in recent weeks. Unai Emery's side were well in contention in December, but since the draw with the Blades, Villa have won only one of their last four. Defeats to Manchester United and Newcastle have knocked them off the pace of the leader and out of the top four, although they can leapfrog Tottenham back into the Champions League places with a win.

They did earn a point in their last home match against West Ham as Ollie McBurnie fired in a stoppage-time penalty. The full-time whistle sounds, and Aston Villa's 11-month unbeaten run in home league games is over! Newcastle halt their own four-match losing run in the competition with an emphatic 3-1 victory on one of the most difficult grounds to visit in the country. Howe's side took a deserved 2-0 lead into half-time thanks to two predatory finishes from Schar, then Gordon, Almiron and Murphy combined on the counterattack to force a Moreno own goal seven minutes after the restart. Villa briefly threatened a comeback when Watkins pulled one back before having a dinked finish chalked off for offside, but the Magpies weathered the storm before seeing out the closing stages in relative comfort. Villa miss the chance to join Arsenal on 46 points, and they could now see their three-point lead over Tottenham wiped out when Ange Postecoglou's men face Brentford on Wednesday. Newcastle, meanwhile, leapfrog Chelsea, Manchester United and Brighton to go seventh with a statement win! That's all from Villa Park, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

It's full-time at Anfield, and Liverpool restore their five-point lead at the top of the Premier League with a crushing 4-1 win over Chelsea. The Reds were utterly dominant in the first half with Jota and Bradley finding the net before Nunez missed a penalty, and that didn't change after the restart! The full-time whistle goes, and every single pre-game script goes up in flames, as Kobbie Mainoo comes to the rescue for Manchester United to secure a desperately late 4-3 victory over Wolves! The visitors' early missed chances in the second half came back to bite them in the 71st minute, as Sarabia slotted in a penalty to give Wolves some hope in the final quarter of the game. A dominant first-half and a chaotic second for Manchester United, who eventually collect all three points at the end of a frankly crazy game which reminds us all just how unpredictable the Premier League can be!

De Bruyne comes off the bench to help City come from behind to beat Newcastle 3-2. The Magpies had a goal disallowed for offside inside 90 seconds, which also resulted in Ederson having to go off injured as he collided with Walker trying to make the save. City are aiming to try and close the gap to leaders Liverpool to just two points, with the Reds not playing until next weekend. They have a good record against Newcastle though, winning more games (30) and scoring more goals (98) against them than any other opponent in the Premier League.

They did win last time out, beating local rivals Sunderland 3-0 in the FA Cup. Eddie Howe will be hoping they can emulate their 1-0 win over City in the EFL Cup earlier this season though to get them back on track.

That's all she wrote at Goodison Park and it finishes goalless between Everton and Aston Villa. In truth, you have to say it was a fair result - the close nature of the match was reflected in the xG with Everton's 1.13 slightly higher than Villa's 1.11. There were definitely opportunities for both teams to win it, not least for Calvert-Lewin who really should have buried his chance when played through one-on-one at the end of the opening period. Villa did have the ball in the back of the net before that through the excellent Moreno, who was denied after a lengthy VAR check. The second half really failed to ignite and became a bit scrappy and needly, so really a point apiece is a fair reflection of the afternoon's proceedings. It means Everton are one point clear of 18th-placed Luton Town but they have played a game more. Villa, meanwhile, remain third in the table, two back of leaders Liverpool and level with Manchester City in second - both of whom have played one game fewer. Thank you for joining this afternoon!

Liverpool consolidate their position at the Premier League summit after an impressive 4-0 victory over in-form Bournemouth at the Vitality Stadium. The Reds move five points clear of Manchester City, who have a game in hand, while they are as many clear of Aston Villa and Arsenal in a close-run contest from second down to fourth in the league table. The visitors were made to be patient in blustery conditions on the south coast, creating little amid a fairly drab first half that was only of interest due to Kluivert escaping a red card for a lunging challenge on Diaz. Klopp’s men turned on the style in the second period, though, as Nunez opened and closed the scoring either side of a brace for Jota. Salah’s absence was hardly felt by the visitors, who had Jota, Nunez and a fine cameo appearance from Gakpo to thank for a comfortable victory. Liverpool stay ahead of the chasing pack before their next Premier League game at Arsenal on February 4, after an EFL Cup semi-final second leg against Fulham and a FA Cup fourth-round clash with Norwich City. Bournemouth are next against Swansea City in the FA Cup before visiting West Ham on February 1. That is all for now, until next time! Goodbye and thanks for following.

Kilman redirected against Sa’s left-hand post at the other end, though neither team could find a winner. Brighton leapfrog Manchester United into seventh before visiting Sheffield United in the FA Cup fourth round on Saturday. Chelsea secure the three points at Luton, coming away with a 3-2 victory. It was looking like a comfortable day for the Blues after they had opened the scoring through Palmer in the first half, followed by Madueke firing home later before half-time. The Hatters were pushing but failed to have a shot on target in the opening 45 minutes. After the break, Palmer struck once again to give Pochettino's side a 3-0 lead, and the win looked as though it was sealed. However, Barkley found the back of the net with just 10 minutes of normal time remaining. Edwards' men threw everything at it, and Adebayo made it 3-2 in the final few minutes. Despite their best efforts, Luton couldn't find an equaliser, and Chelsea end their winless run of four games away from home. Up next for the Hatters is a home tie in the FA Cup against Bolton Wanderers, while Chelsea host Preston in the same competition. That's all for today, goodbye!

The Blues picked up a 2-1 win over Crystal Palace in the week through a last-minute penalty from Noni Madueke, which may have papered over the cracks of what was a lacklustre performance against a struggling side. Palace's eight-game winless run in the Premier League ended with a 3-1 victory over Brentford at Selhurst Park. The Bees had won their last four away London derbies and took the lead inside two minutes. Jensen flicked the ball down the right to Roerslev, who curled in an accurate first-time cross. Rewarded for resilience and making the most of their chances, Fulham end their losing streak and return to winning ways in their final fixture of 2023; meanwhile, back-to-back defeats leave Arsenal sitting fourth in the Premier League table, when victory at Craven Cottage would have put them top at the turn of the year. The Gunners scored early on through Saka and had most of the ball, but their hosts proved more potent in the final third - Jimenez levelled before the break; De Cordova-Reid then netted from close in - and are merited 2-1 winners. While the Cottagers can enjoy the rest of New Year's Eve, Arteta's men must ponder what has gone wrong in a dismal December. Arsenal lose a top-flight match after opening the scoring for the first time since January 2022, and after 48 games without defeat, that run has now ended. They will host Liverpool in the FA Cup third round next week, while Fulham tackle Championship strugglers Rotherham. That's all from today's live coverage, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Arsenal may have had 68 per cent possession over the final 15 minutes of the first half, when they started to threaten Fulham a little more often, but their response to conceding has not been totally convincing. Will Arteta act decisively, making some personnel changes? Meanwhile, Marco Silva will surely ask for more of the same from his team, who have improved significantly from their dismal showing at Bournemouth.
A relatively even first half ends level at Craven Cottage, where Fulham fought back from conceding an early goal to draw level at 1-1 just before the half-hour mark. Arsenal's early momentum was not maintained, and the visitors found it tough to carve out clear chances following Saka's fifth-minute strike from close range. Their hosts, meanwhile, can be content with showing real spirit, having just lost three straight games without scoring, and Jimenez coolly converted Cairney's cross to deservedly restore parity. There's all to play for after the break, when a win for Arsenal would put them top of the Premier League table.

Two ex-Arsenal players combine, as Iwobi's cross from the right somehow evades several bodies in the box before landing at the feet of Willian. The winger then curls a shot from the left side of the box only a foot or two wide of the right-hand upright!
(16’) Castagne reaches the right byline, but his stood-up cross is too high for Willian in the centre, and Arsenal's towering back four comfortably manage to get the ball away from any danger.
--- 14’ Highlight SAVE! A first-time finish from Jimenez sends Raya scrambling across to make a sharp save, after Robinson delivers a low cross from the left flank towards his team-mate. That's Fulham's first real chance, but they still trail 1-0. ---
(13’) Fulham have actually had marginally more of the ball than their visitors so far, but they've yet to create any openings in Arsenal's rearguard, which has proven less resilient this season.
(11’) Fulham are looking for their first league win over Arsenal for nearly 12 years, having been outscored 29-10 during their winless streak. Today's encounter appears to be going the same way - but there's plenty of time remaining to salvage something from this game.
(9’) A typically tigerish tackle by yellow-card magnet Joao Palhinha sees Havertz upended in midfield, but the referee does not merit it worthy of any further attention. Arsenal are trying to retain possession now, keeping Fulham subdued.
(7’) That's nine goals Fulham have conceded since last scoring themselves, and Arsenal have been quick to punish them today. The Gunners have a record of 11 wins and two draws when scoring first in the Premier League so far this season - can the Cottagers come back into this one, though?

Losing 2-0 at home to West Ham last week ended Arsenal's 10-game unbeaten home run and leaves them fourth, two points behind both leaders Liverpool and second-placed Aston Villa; level with reigning champions Manchester City. At the halfway point of their league campaign, Mikel Arteta's men have accrued 10 fewer points than at this stage of last season. The Gunners have, though, won each of their last five Premier League away games against today's hosts, scoring at least three goals in each of the last four.
Back-to-back 5-0 wins earlier this month took Fulham up the table in some style; however, Marco Silva's side have now lost their last three top-flight matches without scoring, conceding eight goals in the process. As a result, they occupy 14th place on 21 points. Ahead of today's game, the Cottagers have been beaten five times in their last seven Premier League home fixtures against fellow London opposition, failing to score across all five defeats. Following a 2-2 draw with Arsenal in August, they are also still seeking their first league win over the Gunners since January 2012.

The full-time whistle brings this absolute thriller to a close, with Liverpool going three points clear at the Premier League summit with a 4-2 win over Newcastle United! After a chaotic first half somehow ended without a goal, the game continued in the same manner in the second period, Salah scoring the opener before Isak levelled on the break, completely against the run of play. Klopp's team continued to dominate, ultimately racking up 34 shots and 7.27 xG, and goals from Jones and Gakpo looked to have sealed the three points, only for Botman to drag Newcastle back to 3-2 with nine minutes left. However, Salah – who saw a penalty saved in the first half – converted a second spot-kick with four minutes remaining, bowing out with a brace ahead of his trip to the Africa Cup of Nations and finally killing off Howe's visitors. Both teams are in FA Cup action later this week, with Liverpool visiting Arsenal for a heavyweight clash on Sunday after Newcastle – who have now lost five of their last six league games – go to Sunderland for Saturday's Tyne–Wear derby! We hope you've enjoyed our live coverage of this absorbing contest. Until next time, it's goodbye from us!
(90’) FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 4-2 NEWCASTLE UNITED.
(90’) Liverpool's xG figure for this match now stands at a massive 7.27, compared to 0.59 for Newcastle. That is the highest figure ever recorded in a Premier League game, and the Reds are about to move three points clear at the top of the table!
(90’) Nothing comes of Liverpool's corner, but the Reds are back in possession and can stroke it around patiently, with Newcastle a beaten team.
--- 90’ +4 Highlight Chance for 5-2! Salah has Jota in support as he bursts into the box on the right-hand side, but he looks to sign off with a hat-trick ahead of his trip to the Africa Cup of Nations, ignoring his team-mate and cutting inside to shoot. Botman blocks his strike, then Jota sees the follow-up deflected behind. ---
(90’) Newcastle's winless run in Premier League action at Anfield is about to reach 28 games. Everton, with an ongoing run against Chelsea, are the only other team to endure a winless away streak of that length against any opponent in the competition.
(90’) We will have SEVEN minutes of stoppage time at Anfield! Surely there are no further twists to come?
(90’) Salah is the first player to score, assist, miss a penalty and score a penalty in a Premier League game since Wayne Rooney for Everton against Swansea City in February 2017.

(71’) Newcastle have won their first league game in just one of the last 11 calendar years (three draws, seven losses), winning 1-0 at Stoke City in 2018. However, they've never lost against Liverpool on New Year's Day in three previous meetings, drawing 0-0 in 1913 before winning 9-2 in 1934 and 1-0 in 2003. Can they hold out to maintain that record?
(70’) Newcastle, of course, have suffered late heartache twice in recent memory against Liverpool. Fabio Carvalho scored a 98th-minute winner for the Reds in this exact fixture last August, while they lost by the same scoreline when the teams last met at St James Park in August 2023, Nunez netting two late goals off the bench as Klopp's men triumphed on Tyneside with 10 men. Does a similar fate await them here? They are hanging on for dear life!

Despite dominating for large parts at London Stadium, Brighton settle for a goalless draw with fellow top-six hopefuls West Ham in the Premier League. Areola was forced into some eight saves, his most in a league home game since making 10 against Manchester City in September, as the Seagulls controlled proceedings on the road. Substitute Ferguson went close, as did Gross on two occasions, while Moder blazed over a great opportunity towards the end of the second half. As for the Hammers’ attacking chances, Ward-Prowse was denied in the first half by Steele, while Soucek prodded wide after the interval. Moyes will see it as a good point, although this marks a first clean sheet of the season for De Zerbi’s visitors, who move up to seventh in the league table and one place behind the hosts. Both sides now take a break from league action to take part in the FA Cup third round, in which West Ham host Bristol City on Sunday, while Brighton visit Stoke City the day before. That is all for now, until next time – goodbye!

Well, where on earth to start with that one? Luton win 3-2 amidst anarchy at Bramall Lane, seeing their own lead slip midway through the second half before two own-goals in four minutes gifted them the points at Sheffield United's expense!! The Blades meant business in the second period and finally broke through just after the hour mark, McBurnie lashing home after McAtee kept the ball alive in the Hatters' box. Late chances for Osula and Ben Slimane both went awry as the hosts desperately chased a deserved equaliser, but Luton held out to claim all three points and secure a second win in a row. A game that was as mad as a hatter ends in favour of the Hatters themselves, leaving Sheffield United's side rooted to the foot of the Premier League table, and taking Luton just one point away from climbing out of the relegation zone.

Liverpool have two goals chalked off for offside but still manage to secure the three points, beating Burnley at Turf Moor by two goals to nil. Brentford are put out of their misery by the final whistle, with Wolves clinching a memorable 4-1 win at the Gtech Community Stadium, earning back-to-back Premier League victories for the first time this season! Wolves had a commanding lead to defend when the second half began, with Lemina's early header and Hwang's brace putting them 3-1 up as Brentford continually played themselves into trouble. The Bees enjoyed plenty of possession as they looked for a route back into the game, but they couldn't find a way past Wolves' resolute backline and the visitors killed the contest when Collins – who endured a torrid outing – played a terrible pass to Cunha, allowing him to tee up Bellegarde to make it 4-1 on the break. Wolves return to 11th place with 25 points at the halfway stage of the season, while Brentford are looking over their shoulders in 14th, four points clear of the bottom three after losing their fourth straight game. Both teams are back in action on Saturday, with Wolves hosting Everton and Brentford visiting Crystal Palace. Until then, it's goodbye from us – thank you for joining us!

Manchester City return to winning ways in the Premier League as they come from behind to triumph 3-1 over Everton at Goodison Park. Guardiola’s side showed some signs of a Club World Cup hangover as they fell behind to Harrison’s well-taken 29th-minute opener after McNeil capitalised on a Rodri error to tee up that goal. However, the defending English champions responded in scintillating fashion in the second half as Foden rattled in an equaliser from range before Alvarez edged the visitors ahead with a spot-kick. Onana was adjudged to have handled for that penalty decision when blocking Ake’s effort and Pickford almost denied the City forward from 12 yards, too, but the away side did not look back as Silva extended their lead with just four minutes remaining. The Citizens leapfrog Tottenham to go into fourth but still trail top-flight leaders Liverpool by five points, while Everton remain just one clear of 18th-placed Luton Town, who are in the relegation zone but have a game in hand. Sheffield United visit City on Saturday, while the Toffees travel to Wolves on the same day. That is all for now, until next time! Goodbye and thanks for following.

Arsenal miss the chance to return to the Premier League summit after West Ham complete a perfect smash-and-grab performance to win 2-0 against their London rivals at Emirates Stadium. Soucek opened the scoring after just 13 minutes in controversial circumstances as the VAR and referee Oliver concluded Bowen had kept the ball in play when setting up his midfield team-mate. However, Jesus missed two good chances in the second half before Mavropanos headed in against his former side, extending the lead for Moyes’ men to 2-0. Benrahma still saw a 96th-minute penalty saved by Raya, though that will matter for little as West Ham jump up to sixth in the league, while Arteta’s side remain two points behind top-flight leaders Liverpool. Solanke scored a second-half hat-trick to help Bournemouth come from behind to beat Forest 3-2 in a controversial match at the City Ground. Bournemouth will aim to make it six wins in seven games when they host Fulham in their next outing. As for Forest, they are just two points above the relegation zone and travel to Newcastle United next. That's all for today, goodbye.

Having wasted numerous chances, Manchester City turn to their star striker to edge them to victory over battling Brentford, with a 1-0 win taking the champions within a point of Liverpool at the Premier League summit. When the Bees finally lost their discipline midway through the second half, City countered at speed, and Haaland coolly found the bottom corner to finally beat Flekken. The Dutch goalkeeper remained defiant throughout, but that one lapse allows Guardiola's side to win their ninth home game in the league this season and places more pressure on the leaders, who host Luton Town tomorrow. Meanwhile, City will visit Bournemouth on Saturday, and beaten Brentford tackle West Ham in six days time, still needing points to preserve their top-flight status. That's all from today's live coverage, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Sheffield United belatedly earned both their second win and first clean sheet of the Premier League season last weekend: the Blades beat Brentford 1-0 but are still bottom of the table on goal difference.
