The full-time whistle blows at St James' Park as Newcastle celebrate a much-needed 3-0 victory over 10-man Fulham. It was comfortable in the end, though the visitors did put up a decent fight after Jimenez saw red 22 minutes in for a bizarre challenge on Longstaff. Silva's men made it to the break level, but their resistance was broken with 57 minutes on the clock as persistent work from Guimaraes ended with Miley lashing home for his first ever senior Newcastle goal. Almiron made it 2-0 not long after, before Burn made the points safe on his return from injury as he bundled home Guimaraes' cross at the second attempt. Howe's men win for the first time in four games in all competitions, moving them onto 29 points and ahead of Manchester United. The victory comes at some cost, though, with Schar and Joelinton both limping off, worsening the Magpies' already horrendous injury crisis. Fulham remain on 21 points, still 12 points above the bottom three. They will look to get back on track when they travel to Goodison Park to take on Everton in the EFL Cup quarter-final on Tuesday, while Newcastle will look to reach the last four of that competition when they visit Chelsea the same day. That is all we have for you from St James' Park, so thanks for your company and goodbye!

Pressure has mounted on Erik ten Hag in recent weeks, despite the United boss winning the Premier League’s Manager of the Month for November. Ten Hag’s men still sat sixth in the league table heading into this weekend’s fixtures, although pockets of United supporters appear to be getting frustrated – this game will be pivotal for the Manchester visitors, who need to banish their Anfield demons to keep the noise down around Ten Hag’s future at Old Trafford.

However, victory for Arsenal against Brighton and an ill-tempered win for Aston Villa over Brentford earlier on Sunday saw Jurgen Klopp’s side drop to third before kick-off at Anfield. Liverpool were, of course, 7-0 winners in this exact fixture last season and would regain top spot with another derby triumph.

Forest and their boss Steve Cooper, meanwhile, are entering the last chance saloon here. Many expected Cooper to be sacked after his team were humiliated in a 5-0 defeat at Fulham in midweek, and if reports are to be believed, another loss here would spell the end for the popular Forest coach. The visitors sit four points clear of the relegation zone after losing four Premier League games on the spin, and the patience of tripper-happy owner Evangelos Marinakis seems to be wearing thin.
Gary O'Neil's Wolves are targeting two home wins in the space of four days after overcoming Burnley on this ground on Tuesday, when Hwang Hee-chan's eighth Premier League goal of the season gave them a hard-fought 1-0 win over the Clarets. Arsenal were the last side to come away from Villa Park with three points after their 4-2 win back in February. They're in good form themselves and they're looking to go back to the top of the table with another victory here after Liverpool's win over Crystal Palace earlier today. They've won their last six on the bounce in all competitions, extending that run in dramatic fashion as Declan Rice's stoppage-time goal snatched a 4-3 win over Luton Town on Tuesday.

The full-time whistle sparks more jubilant Goodison Park celebrations as Everton clinch a 2-0 victory against a disappointing Chelsea side. The first half was a low-key affair, but Doucoure's 54th-minute goal gave Everton life and something to defend. They had to do a lot of that, though they rarely looked seriously troubled by the visitors' tame attack, and the points were made safe in added time as 20-year-old substitute Dobbin lashed home for his first senior goal for the club to put the game to bed. The win extends Everton's gap to the bottom three to four points, and they will look to continue their great form when they travel to struggling Burnley next Saturday. For Chelsea, another poor performance and results elsewhere mean they drop to 12th, and they will hope to put in a better display when they host relegation-threatened Sheffield United next weekend. That is all we have from Goodison Park, so thanks for your company and goodbye!

Tottenham finally return to winning ways in some style. They were beaten home and away by Newcastle last season but outclassed them this time, scoring in the first half through Udogie and Richarlison after fine work from Son. Richarlison got another just when Newcastle were looking for a route back into the match in the second period, then Son got a deserved goal for himself from the penalty spot after he was fouled by Dubravka. Newcastle could have scored early but ultimately had to settle for Joelinton's consolation. As Spurs look forward to Friday's trip to Nottingham Forest, Newcastle must first lift themselves to play Milan in the Champions League. That is all from this game. Goodbye!

Tottenham will hope they turned a corner in that first half, while Newcastle have a mountain to climb. They have lost 55 of the previous 56 Premier League away games in which they have been two or more goals down at half-time, recovering to take a point only against Liverpool in 2016.
The first big chance may have gone Newcastle's way, when Isak could not convert, but it has been one-way traffic since then. Tottenham are 2-0 up after two very similar goals. Twice Son ran at Trippier, twice he made space for a cross, and twice he found a team-mate for a first-time finish. Udogie got the opener, but Spurs have had no trouble netting first. The vital goal will perhaps be the second, which Richarlison grabbed to give Tottenham a commanding half-time lead.

This is the first meeting between Luton Town and Arsenal in any competition since December 1991, with the Hatters prevailing 1-0 at Kenilworth Road. They would certainly take a repeat of that today in this tussle between sides with contrasting ambitions for the campaign. We are now just a few moments away from kick-off.
Arsenal show three changes from their 2-1 win over Wolves on Saturday. Two of those alterations come in defence - or more specifically at full-back - as White and Kiwior replace Zinchenko and Takehiro Tomiyasu, the latter of whom is not in the squad. Havertz also returns to the starting line-up in place of the benched Trossard. Academy product Walters, yet to make his senior debut, is among the defensive cover on the bench.
Edwards has made four changes to the Luton XI from their loss at Brentford three days ago. Brown has scored in his last two matches as a substitute and is handed a start in attack, while Adebayo is also restored to the frontline, with Ogbene and Morris dropping down to the bench. Former Tottenham winger Townsend and fit-again Doughty are the other two recalled players, taking the places of Chong and injured skipper Tom Lockyer, who is not in the squad.

Rob Edwards' men lost 3-1 away to Brentford at the weekend, but they have drawn with Liverpool and beaten Crystal Palace in their past two home matches. Goals from Marcos Senesi and Kieffer More saw Bournemouth extend their Premier League unbeaten streak to four games as they won 2-0 away against Crystal Palace. The visitors took a deserved lead midway through the first half when Senesi headed home from a corner and looked comfortable in defence as Palace tried to claw back an equaliser after the break. Moving back within two points of Arsenal at the Premier League summit, below-par Liverpool see off struggling Sheffield United and secure a 2-0 victory with goals late in either half. Van Dijk and Szoboszlai both converted coolly from close range to make the Reds' dominance of possession pay, while their hosts battled bravely without posing much threat in the final third. This result extends Liverpool's unbeaten run in the top flight to its eighth game, and they will aim to prolong such a streak on Saturday, when in the second of three straight away fixtures they visit Selhurst Park to meet Crystal Palace. Meanwhile, the beaten Blades host Brentford this weekend, with Wilder hoping to get off the mark in his second spell as United boss. That's all from Bramall Lane today, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Villa's winning run at home stretches to 14 games as they shone in a 1-0 victory over City. It was a magnificent performance by Emery's man from start to finish, with City not knowing what hit them. Villa had 13 shots alone in the first 45 minutes, the most against a Guardiola team in the first half of a match in Europe's big five leagues, with Ederson having to make big saves to keep his side in it. Martinez also made a brilliant double save to deny Haaland, which were City's only shots in the whole match. It took until the 74th minute for the deadlock to be broken, with Bailey's deflected shot wrongfooting Ederson. Luiz also hit the post late on with a long-range strike. It's a huge win for the Villains as it lifts them above City into third, and they have another big game at home against Arsenal on Saturday. It's now four without a win in the league for City, who are six points off leaders Arsenal. They travel to Luton Town at the weekend. That's all for today, goodbye!

It was a familiar story for Wolves and Gary O'Neil on Monday, as they were beaten by a stoppage-time penalty on a second successive Premier League road trip, going down 3-2 to Fulham. Marco Silva's team were awarded two questionable penalties and were perhaps fortunate to keep 11 men on the pitch in that game, leading O'Neil to say he had "finally turned against" the use of VAR in his post-match interview. He'll be hoping there is no controversy awaiting Wolves here, but they face a daunting task, taking on the leaders without suspended midfield duo Mario Lemina and Joao Gomes.
With Manchester City not in action until Sunday, Arsenal have a chance to end Saturday four points clear at the summit as they bid to improve on last season's second-place finish! That will give huge motivation to Mikel Arteta's team, who had to dig deep last week for a 1-0 win at Brentford. They then warmed up for this contest in brilliant fashion in midweek, hammering Lens 6-0 in the UEFA Champions League after racing into a five-goal lead by half-time – a similar performance here would certainly be welcomed by the Gunners' fans!
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League fixture from the Emirates Stadium, as leaders Arsenal welcome Wolves to north London!

Following a tepid first half, devoid of either chances or inspiration, scoring three of four goals during the second sees Brentford return to winning ways at Luton Town's expense. The Bees totally dominated possession, and when they added a clinical edge shortly after the interval, that was enough to take them two goals clear heading into the final 15 minutes. Luton's late strike threatened to set up a grandstand finale, but when Baptiste finished decisively from close range, all three points were wrapped up for Thomas Frank's side, who now move into the top half of the Premier League table. Still waiting for their first clean sheet of the season, the Hatters host in-form Arsenal on Tuesday, while Brentford travel south to Brighton one day later. That's all from West London today, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!

Having inched further clear of the relegation zone with their first-ever Premier League home victory, Luton now tackle a side that have dominated them for several years: they've lost on five of their last six visits to Brentford, where they last tasted success some 21 years ago.

Burnley thumped 10-man United 5-0 to secure their first home win in the Premier League this season. The Clarets started the game as they meant to go on, with Rodriguez heading in Taylor's cross from the left inside the first 15 seconds. Bruun Larsen touched down O'Shea's long pass forward before scoring double their lead, with Archer shooting over for the Blades soon after. McBurnie was then given two yellow cards for separate elbows on O'Shea just before the break. The hosts dominated from that point and netted three goals inside seven minutes. Amdouni rushed through two defenders and slotted in his shot to net Burnley's third before setting up Koleosho, who found the near post with his low strike. Captain Brownhill got in on the act and curled in the fifth and final goal. He arrived on the edge of the box and whipped his strike into the corner of the net. Redmond went close late on, but the substitute rattled the bar with his flicked header. Next up, Burnley will look to build on their win when they head to Wolves. As for the Blades, they host Liverpool. That's all for today, goodbye.

The Blades finished second in the Championship last season, nine points behind league winners Burnley. However, they have also struggled since gaining promotion to the Premier League. Paul Heckingbottom’s side lost nine of their first 10 games in the top flight, with their only point coming against Everton. Vincent Kompany’s side have only collected four points this campaign, drawing with Nottingham Forest and beating Luton Town. Ten-man Chelsea hold on to get a vital home win as they beat Brighton 3-2. The Blues made a perfect start to the game, with two corners causing Brighton all sorts of problems. Fernandez headed in his first Premier League goal from the first, while Colwill thumped in his first Chelsea goal to double their tally. That lead was halved just before the break, with Buonanotte curling in a wonderful strike before Gallagher received his second yellow card. Fernandez got his second of the game in the 65th minute from the spot after Milner fouled Mudryk, and it took Brighton until stoppage time to pull back another, with Pedro flicking it in at the near post. In the dying moments, the referee awarded a spot-kick to the Seagulls for handball, but it was overturned by VAR. It's a win that lifts Chelsea into 10th, and they'll be hoping to build some momentum off this as they travel to Manchester United on Wednesday. Brighton stay in eighth, with Brentford at home next up for them. That's all for today, goodbye!

Spurs were flying high after 10 matchdays, sitting top of the table after a stellar unbeaten start to the season. Since then, they've lost three on the bounce, taking the lead in all of those matches only to come away with no points. It's a run that's seen them drop to sixth in the table, but a win here would move them level on points with today's opponents. Spurs have the best winning record against Pep Guardiola's City, winning six of their meetings, however, only one of those victories has come at the Etihad - a 3-2 win in February 2022.
City have the chance to close the gap at the top of the league back to one point with a win here after Arsenal's victory over Wolves yesterday. The Citizens are unbeaten in eight matches in all competitions (W6 D2), but have drawn their last two Premier League games, dropping leads against both Chelsea and Liverpool, with the latter bringing an end to their 23-game winning run at the Etihad. They come into today on the back of a win though, coming from 2-0 down to beat RB Leipzig 3-2 and claim top spot in their Champions League group.

Chris Kavanagh brings this game to an end as Liverpool fight back to claim a 1-1 draw at the home of the champions! The Reds looked set to fall four points behind City when Haaland scored his 50th Premier League goal in the first half, swivelling on Ake's pass to finish after a poor kick out from Alisson. Chances came at a premium during a low-key second half, with Dias seeing a potential second goal chalked off by the VAR as Akanji was adjudged to have fouled Alisson, while Ederson got down to deny Nunez at his near post at the other end. However, Liverpool avoided their second defeat of the Premier League season as Alexander-Arnold capped an impressive performance with a great finish into the bottom-left corner, with Haaland's header drifting just wide at the death as City failed to find a winner. That result keeps City one point clear of the Reds at the summit, also opening the door for Arsenal to finish the day top of the table if they can beat Brentford later on Saturday. Both teams are back in European action next week, with City hosting RB Leipzig in the Champions League while Liverpool face LASK in the Europa League. Until then, it's goodbye from us. Villa complete a sensational turnaround to take all three points from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, condemning their hosts to a third straight defeat in the process! Spurs made another fast start in the second half, with Lo Celso, Gil, Johnson and Son all going close within 15 minutes of the resumption, the latter denied by the offside flag after scoring. In the ascendancy for much of that first half, Spurs find themselves level despite a plethora of scoring chances. Kulusevski has led the charge, striking the post with an early attempt and having another off-target, as well as creating a big chance for Gil. The Spaniard forced a save from Martinez, while also completing a whopping 13 final-third passes and completing two of his three dribbles as Spurs tore through Villa's defence at times. Can they find even more of those gaps as the second half progresses?
Well, what about that for a first half of Premier League football? This game has had absolutely everything so far, with Spurs racing out of the traps like a team possessed. A flurry of early chances came and went for Udogie, Kulusevski, Gil, Son and Porro, before a corner from the latter fell for Lo Celso. The midfielder struck home a deflected half-volley, but the celebrations hadn't even died down before Villa went straight up the other end and scored what looked like the equaliser. A lengthy VAR check ruled Watkins' deft header to have come from an offside position, and the visitors were back to chasing the game, although Spurs continued to have chances of their own through Kulusevski before Son was too denied by the flag after putting the ball in the net. A late free-kick would prove to be Villa's trump card though, as defender Torres' bullet header found the top corner - and this time, crucially, stood. It's been played at breakneck speed so far with goals, disallowed goals, chances and challenges aplenty all over the pitch, and we're in for another treat if the second half is anywhere near as frenetic.

Willian's stoppage-time penalty ends Fulham's winless run as they beat Wolves 3-2. It was an even first half, which ended with the teams level at 1-1. There's just one change by Gary O'Neil to his side after their win over Spurs last time out, and it's an enforced one. Craig Dawson is suspended, so he's replaced by Santiago Bueno, who has recovered from an ankle injury. Lemina and Semedo have both overcome injuries of their own to start, while Doherty is fit enough for the bench after a hamstring issue.
Marco Silva makes two changes from the loss to Aston Villa two weeks ago, with Reed and Cairney both coming into the side. Jimenez, who scored his first Fulham goal in that game, retains his place against his former side and Leno makes his 150th Premier League appearance. De Cordova-Reid drops to the bench, while Joao Palhinha is suspended for accumulating five bookings this season.

As for Wolves, after a slightly slow start to their own season, they're hitting their stride now. They've lost just one of their last seven Premier League outings (W3 D3), though that defeat did come in their last away trip as they had a controversial penalty awarded against them in the dying moments which saw Sheffield United beat them 2-1. Wolves come into this game on the back of an outstanding stoppage-time comeback which saw them beat Tottenham 2-1 before the international break.
Compared to their heights of last season, Fulham have made an inconsistent start to this campaign, coming into this game sitting in 15th place with just 12 points so far. They've won just three of their Premier League games so far (D3 L6), and are without a win in their last four outings in the competition, drawing one and losing the other three. Two of those victories have come at home, including their most recent - a 3-1 win over Sheffield United - though that was back at the start of October.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Fulham and Wolves at Craven Cottage!

And breathe! The full-time whistle sparks more wild celebrations at Molineux, where Wolves have scored two stoppage-time goals to condemn Tottenham to back-to-back defeats in the most remarkable fashion! Johnson's early tap-in looked like being enough for Postecoglou's men as Wolves squandered chance after chance, with Hwang and Kalajdzic guilty of their two most glaring misses in the second half. However, the late introduction of Sarabia was the catalyst for a stunning turnaround. The Spaniard levelled with a brilliant strike as the clock ticked into stoppage-time, then turned provider in the 97th minute as his low cross was turned home by Lemina! What a result for O'Neil's team – it's just the eighth time a team has won a Premier League game when they were losing going into the 90th minute, and half of those matches have involved Tottenham (two wins, two losses). Wolves go into the international break on a high with 15 points from 12 games, and they will face Fulham at Craven Cottage after the hiatus. Spurs, meanwhile, must regroup ahead of a huge showdown with Aston Villa at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on November 26. Thank you for joining us for our coverage of another crazy Premier League game – it's goodbye for now, and we'll see you next time!

Arsenal are back to winning ways in the Premier League with a 3-1 victory over Burnley. It took the Gunners a long time to break their opponents down, with Trossard nodding them in front from close range just before half-time. Relentless in their dominance at fortress Villa Park, Aston Villa post a 13th straight home win in the Premier League, seeing off struggling Fulham despite performing a little below their best. Unai Emery's side cruised to a two-goal lead at half-time, but even after extending their advantage with a rapid counter-attack, their visitors continued to test them and deservedly notched a consolation strike as Jimenez scored his first league goal for well over a year. The Villans start a league campaign with six successive home victories for the first time since 1959, and they will resume with a tough test at Tottenham after the international break. Liverpool jump up to third in the Premier League after a 3-0 victory over Brentford at Anfield. Salah opened the scoring with his well-taken 39th-minute strike, punishing the Bees for failing to take their chances before half-time. Nunez had twice seen goals ruled out for offside prior to the opening goal, but will take some comfort from assisting the breakthrough before the interval. Cruising to victory, Klopp introduced Diaz for his first Anfield appearance since his father was released from captivity after being kidnapped in Colombia. The Reds move level on points with the top two, Arsenal and Manchester City – the latter of whom visit Chelsea later on Sunday and will look to make use of their game in hand. The international break offers club football the chance to pause, with Klopp’s men next travelling to Pep Guardiola’s champions on November 25, when Brentford host Arsenal. That is all for now, until next time – goodbye!

It's all over, and Newcastle hold out by the barest of margins to sneak to a 1-0 victory over Arsenal! A close-run, scrappy game was settled by an even scrappier goal, with Gordon's close-range tap-in requiring a five-minute VAR check before being given the green light. After both he and Murphy fluffed chances to score either side of Rice heading wide for Arsenal, Gordon's 63rd minute tap-in was a just reward for Newcastle, who improved significantly from a flat first-half performance. Arsenal piled on the pressure as they chased an equaliser, but couldn't test Pope in any meaningful way as the Magpies' defence held firm to condemn the Gunners to a first Premier League defeat of the season. Three points in a game that was far from black and white take Newcastle up two places into sixth, while Arsenal remain third having missed the chance to potentially go top of the table. They fail to close the gap on the top two, with arch-rivals Tottenham now the only side yet to lose a game in this season's top-flight.

Villa beat Luton 3-1 in their last outing to claim their 12th successive home win in the Premier League, strengthening their grip on fifth place. They have been victorious in five of their previous six top-flight matches since losing to Liverpool at Anfield, with their only draw in that run coming against Wolves. Many had thought Unai Emery's men would struggle to balance their domestic commitments with the relentless Europa Conference League schedule. However, their impressive run of form has seen them collect 22 points from their first 10 matches, their most since the 1998-99 season. If they can secure their eighth league win of the new campaign, they will temporarily move into third place, with Liverpool playing later today.
Forest beat Chelsea at the start of September to move up to ninth position in the Premier League but have since dropped to 16th after a six-game winless run. Despite only losing to Manchester City and Liverpool in that time, Steve Cooper will be disappointed that his side dropped points against early strugglers Burnley and Luton Town, with the two newly promoted clubs in the relegation zone. As a result, the Tricky Trees are just five points above the bottom three and will be hoping that they can turn their form around. They are unbeaten in their previous seven matches at the City Ground but will have to claim a rare win over Villa if they want to move up the table. Forest have only won one of their last 15 against them (drawing seven and losing seven), with their only victory in that run being a 2-1 home win in the Championship back in 2017.

It's all over at Villa Park, as the hosts make their dominance count to seal a comfortable three points. Spurning several chances in the game's first 45 minutes, Villa wasted no time in the second as Diaby doubled their lead with a low drive from close range. Already 2-0 up with the second period just four minutes old, Unai Emery's side looked to push the envelope and again went close through Watkins, before Luton captain Lockyer accidentally turned the ball into his own net for 3-0. That didn't stem the flow of chances though, with Kabore making a crucial challenge to deny Bailey before both the Jamaican and captain McGinn blazed wide from close range. Another own goal would give Luton some parity late in the game, following some slapstick defending from Konsa and Martinez, but despite Mendi and Adebayo having opportunities to close the gap further, the Hatters were thoroughly second-best throughout and lost 3-1 to a Villa side who are proving to be this season's surprise package. Other results keep the Villans in fifth, just a point outside the Champions League places, while Luton remain languishing in 18th following their seventh defeat of the season.

City and their depth of world-class talent are once again fighting at the Premier League summit, sitting in third with the opportunity to cut league-leading Tottenham’s advantage to two points with a victory here. However, back-to-back defeats against Wolves and Arsenal – the latter a fellow title challenger – dampened the mood in Pep Guardiola’s camp before the pause for international football. That dour outlook will have perhaps eased after a 2-1 win over Brighton and a 3-1 victory at Young Boys in the Champions League, as last season’s treble winners aim for three wins on the spin with a visit to their noisy neighbours at Old Trafford.
So long in City’s shadow across recent years, United’s start to the season has befitted their second-rate status in the reckoning between the two Manchester sides. Four wins and as many draws before the international break was hardly enough for a top-four challenge, never mind a first top-flight title since 2012. Erik ten Hag’s men have somewhat improved since, though, defeating struggling Sheffield United 2-1 to back up their late rescue act against Brentford before the October internationals. Unlikely victors in this exact meeting last season, United will be desperate for a derby-day victory to kickstart their season.

Salah's late double helps Liverpool to a 2-0 win over 10-man Everton. Calvert-Lewin could've made things very different if his first-minute header wasn't saved by Alisson, but the game was dominated by the Reds after that. Young was sent off just 37 minutes in for a second yellow card, but Liverpool still struggled to break the visitors down. The hosts also could've been down to 10 after the break, but Konate somehow managed to avoid a second booking. VAR then awarded a penalty for a handball against Keane, which Salah confidently rifled in, and the Egyptian then finished off a counter-attack in the 97th minute to seal the points. Once again, the Cherries' talisman Solanke found a neat finish to put them in front, and the visitors have failed to truly test Neto at the other end. Before today's game, no team had conceded more first-half goals in the Premier League than Bournemouth, so Iraola will be relieved to keep a clean sheet thus far; O'Neil has plenty of thinking to do at the break.

Wolves may have won just one of their six away games against Bournemouth in the league, but they are unbeaten at the Vitality Stadium in Premier League fixtures. After a run of six losses from eight top-flight matches, the West Midlands club have since gone undefeated in their last three, most recently playing out a 1-1 draw with Aston Villa before international football intervened. However, they have won just one of their last 12 away games in the league ahead of today's contest, in which head coach Gary O’Neil reconvenes with his former employers.
Still seeking their first Premier League victory of the season, Bournemouth are one of only two teams yet to win in the English top flight this term. The Cherries have recently suffered three successive league defeats, conceding nine goals in the process; with a 3-0 loss at Everton deepening their woes just before the international break. Indeed, Andoni Iraola's side have scored as many goals in two EFL Cup games as in eight league matches so far (five). While Bournemouth have won just one of their six Premier League meetings with Wolves, it was the clubs' most recent encounter, at Molineux in February.

Brentford get back to winning ways as they cruise to a 3-0 victory over 10-man Burnley. Maupay thought he'd given the Bees the lead inside 10 minutes, only for it to be chalked out for an offside in the build-up. Wissa did get them in front though, tapping in from close range. The Red Devils have underwhelmed this campaign, already trailing fourth-placed Liverpool by five points ahead of this weekend’s fixtures, after winning four and losing as many from their opening eight games.
The Blades have endured a tough start to their top-flight return, sitting at the bottom of the table. Paul Heckingbottom’s side are yet to win in the league and have just one point after eight games. The United players stay out to soak up the atmosphere at Old Trafford, where McTominay has played the role of super-sub to fire the Red Devils to a potentially season-defining result. They move up to ninth in the Premier League table with four wins and four losses this term, while Brentford slump to 14th. Frank's men are now winless in eight games across all competitions.
Wow. What a difference four minutes can make. United were starring down the barrel of a third successive home defeat in the Premier League, one which may have had huge implications for Ten Hag's future, after Onana failed to keep Jensen's shot out in the first half. However, McTominay's late introduction proved the turning point, with the Scot levelling in the 93rd minute with a close-range volley, before beating Strakosha with a 97th-minute header to provoke wild celebrations. It's absolutely gutting for Brentford, but what a relief for United!

Liverpool are yet to lose in all competitions so far this season, winning all seven of their outings since an opening day draw with Chelsea. They've won their last four on the bounce by a 3-1 scoreline and had to come from behind for the fifth time already this campaign to knock Leicester City out of the EFL Cup when they met on Wednesday. A win here today would take the Reds to the top of the table after Manchester City's loss earlier on.

Three points here would lift them above Liverpool, but that means doing something they've only managed once in the last 21 meetings between these sides, and that win came back in October 2017 (4-1), though it was at home.

Dominguez was fortunate to avoid conceding a penalty for handball in the first half, and replays also show that Turner may have caught Wissa inside the box early in the second period…

Fulham won this exact fixture 3-0 last season, but haven't won consecutive away league games against Crystal Palace since a run of three between 1974 and 1978. Both teams are now on the pitch and they are ready to get started.

Fulham have an identical record to their London rivals and are only behind Roy Hodgson’s side on goal difference. The Cottagers also started their campaign with a win after beating Everton before going on a three-game winless run. An enthralling 2-2 draw with Arsenal came between two heavy defeats, with Marco Silva overseeing a 3-0 loss to Brentford and a 5-1 defeat to Manchester City. However, confidence will be back after a victory in their last match. Carlos Vinicius netted his fourth goal in six games in a 1-0 triumph over Luton Town, netting the winner just three minutes after coming off the bench.
Palace lost just one of their opening four Premier League fixtures before falling to defeat against Aston Villa in their previous outing. The Eagles have seven points on the board after securing wins over early struggles Sheffield United and Wolves and a draw versus Brentford, with their only beating coming at the hands of Arsenal. The hosts came close to extending their unbeaten run to four matches at Villa Park and were leading until 87th-minute when Jhon Duran scored the equaliser. Douglas Luiz and Leon Bailey then netted in stoppage time to complete the comeback for Unai Emery’s men. Palace will want to return to winning ways, but they have failed to beat Fulham in their last three encounters (drawing two and losing one).

Luton remain bottom of the pile with a single point to their name, though they will go above Burnley if the Clarets lose to Manchester United in Saturday's late kick-off. Wolves, meanwhile, jump above Bournemouth into 15th place with four points from six matches. After their midweek EFL Cup exertions, Luton visit Everton and Wolves host champions Manchester City!
The full-time whistle sounds at Kenilworth Road, and while Luton have their first point as a Premier League club, they may well see this 1-1 draw as a missed opportunity! The Hatters played over 50 minutes with a numerical advantage after Bellegarde was dismissed for a petulant kick, but they failed to make the most of their dominance. Wolves threatened to take all three points when Neto scored a brilliant solo goal on the break, but Luton hit back through Morris' penalty. Wolves will feel aggrieved by the award of that spot-kick, with the ball striking Gomes' foot before deflecting onto his hand.

Villa upped the ante with their numerical advantage and took the lead through a counter as Ollie Watkins buried his chance on the break. The Blues' problems in goal persisted as they failed to find the back of the net for the third game on the bounce and have now only taken one point out of a possible nine from their last three matches. Villa move up to sixth with their victory.

Richarlison's introduction late in the game proved to be the difference-maker for Ange Postecoglou, as the Brazilian bagged the goal and assist which rescued the points. Brought on with just 10 minutes of normal time to go, Richarlison headed home an equaliser with just 0.12 xG behind it, and laid on the assist for Kulusevski's winner with his only key pass. Three of five aerial duels won in just over 25 minutes on the pitch was crucial for keeping the ball deep in the final third, and that late cameo is the exact performance Richarlison needed to re-gain confidence in his football.
What a finish to this Premier League fixture, as 117 pulsating minutes end with three Tottenham points. Well into stoppage time, Spurs were 1-0 down thanks to Gustavo Hamer's well-taken opener in the 73rd minute, but a raft of late substitutions made all the impact late on. The game was thrown into chaos after Richarlison equalised for Spurs, and he popped up again two minutes later to set up Dejan Kulusevski's winner. With the Spurs fans in a frenzy and both sets of players out on their feet, three more yellow cards, including a second for Oli McBurnie, were shown, as Spurs held on in a 2-1 win which will live long in the memory.

It is also the first encounter between the two sides in any division since February 2016 – the Clarets won that Championship encounter 1-0 at Turf Moor. Ready for the next edition? Hudson-Odoi and Sangare – signed from Chelsea and PSV respectively on deadline day – come in for their debuts, while World Cup winner Montiel and ex-Manchester United winger Elanga are in from the start. It's all over in west London, with the spoils shared at the end of a fiercely contested game. Brentford couldn't follow up Schade's first-half screamer with another goal, although Janelt, Mbeumo and Onyeka all had the opportunity to do so. West Ham remain unbeaten and move top of the Premier League, until Sunday at least, having picked up seven points from three matches. City's Premier League title defence is off to a winning start as they claim a comfortable 3-0 triumph over newly promoted Burnley at Turf Moor. The goalkeeper denied Maupay and Doucoure with outstanding saves, while Patterson hit the crossbar with the goal gaping. Everton created chance after chance, but they couldn't take them!

Striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the big-name absentee for Everton, having failed to recover from a hamstring injury in time to make the Toffees' season opener. Maupay deputises for him up front, while Young, ironically, becomes the oldest outfielder to debut for a Premier League side since Kevin Phillips (40 years, 24 days) at Crystal Palace in August 2013, at the age of 38 years and 34 days.

Since they last met Brentford in May, when the Bees stung their hosts with a 3-1 win, much has changed at Tottenham. The post-Harry Kane era begins here, as Spurs also play their first competitive fixture under Ange Postecoglou. The departure of their talisman and leading goalscorer comes after an eighth-placed finish last term and defeat in their final friendly of pre-season, which saw them beaten by Barcelona on Tuesday. Nonetheless, the Lilywhites have lost their first league game just once in the last seven years, winning on five occasions.
While Brentford have won just two of their opening league games over the past 11 seasons, they have not lost either of their two Premier League openers to date. Since promotion in 2021, the Bees have beaten Arsenal and held Leicester City to a 2-2 draw. Thomas Frank's side finished just one point and one place behind their opponents here in last term's final standings, having posted five wins from their final six games. Though unbeaten throughout their last nine capital-city fixtures in the Premier League - winning each of the last four in a row - Brentford have a miserable record against Tottenham: they have won only two of the teams' 10 league meetings.
